title: Avoiding a target state across a machine seam
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be deterministic Turing machines with $k$ work tapes over Boolean symbols, with state sets $S$ and $R$, respectively; choose a state $leave\in S$, a state $enter\in R$, and a target state in $S\oplus R$. For a Boolean input $x$, configurations $d,e$ of $A$ on $x$, and times $t,v\in\mathbb N$, suppose $A$ runs from $d$ to $e$ in $t$ steps, $e$ is in state $leave$, and $leave$ is not visited at any earlier time. Suppose also that the configurations of this run, relabeled into the left side of $S\oplus R$, never have the target state through time $t$, and that the run of $B$ from $e$ with its state replaced by $enter$, relabeled into the right side, avoids the target state for its first $v$ steps. Then the machine that runs $A$ until $leave$ and continues with $B$ from $enter$ avoids the target state for every time strictly less than $t+1+v$, when started from $d$ relabeled into the left side.
hypotheses_covered: $k\in\mathbb N$, $S,R$ are types, and $S$ has decidable equality
$leave\in S$, $enter\in R$, and a target state in $S\oplus R$
$d,e$ are configurations of $A$ on input $x$ and $t,v\in\mathbb N$
the left-relabeled run avoids the target through time $t$
the right-relabeled run from $e$ with state replaced by $enter$ avoids the target for times below $v$
